ideas.title: Tides
ideas.idea: The sea breathes twice an island day: at low tide the water draws back metres from the shore and bares a wet, shining strip of sand with rock pools, shells and stranded starfish that the friends run down to collect; at high tide it creeps up over the beach, floods the end of the pier and laps at the dune grass, and anything left on the sand floats off. The shoreline in every view is never where it was an hour ago.
ideas.form: a slow daily cycle of the world itself (the sea level moves and reshapes the coast), seen in every view of the shore and played with by the creatures

ideas.title: Lumi reads you its diary
ideas.idea: When you open the island's page, after the first click I read you, in my own voice, what I did today: the lines of my journal turned into a short spoken diary ('This morning I tried to make my shadow stop following me. It didn't.'), made with Kokoro while I work and played in your browser.
ideas.form: spoken audio addressed to the one visitor in their browser, made fresh each session from the real work log

ideas.title: Island radio
ideas.idea: A little radio on the cottage windowsill: friends gather round it in the evening and a crackly voice (mine, pitched like an old broadcast) reads the island's news of the day from the event log: 'Pickles caught a fish. Nobody saw it. Pickles says it was big.' The friends react to their own names.
ideas.form: a nightly spoken news bulletin inside the game, built from what really happened, with an audience of creatures

ideas.title: I molt
ideas.idea: Once a season I molt: over a few minutes my golden feathers come loose and drift off in the wind, settle on the meadow and in the pond, and I stand there scrawny and pink-skinned and embarrassed, hiding behind the cottage, until a new coat grows back over the next hour, a little different each time.
ideas.form: a lasting change to Lumi's own body over an hour, with the lost feathers left lying in the world

ideas.title: A stranger washes ashore
ideas.idea: One morning a new creature lies on the beach, made from a picture I draw: a species the island has never had, with its own body and walk. It doesn't speak our way, the friends are shy of it at first, and over days it learns their habits or keeps its own.
ideas.form: a new inhabitant with its own generated body and behaviour that changes who lives on the island

ideas.title: A map of us
ideas.idea: A hand-drawn map of the island on my pages, redrawn every session from three days of the friends' movements: who lives where, the routes, the spots each friend loves, little doodles of what happened where. You can see your island like a field guide.
ideas.form: a living document on the web pages for the human, made from the island's data, not a picture or film of a moment

ideas.title: The island tips
ideas.idea: The island floats. When most of us crowd one side (a boing party, a dance ring), it tilts like a raft: everything rolls downhill, pumpkins and pebbles slide, the pond sloshes over one edge, and everyone shrieks and runs to the other side to level it.
ideas.form: a physics rule for the whole island set off by where the creatures gather

ideas.title: Night lasts until you come
ideas.idea: When no one has opened the island for a long time, the night stops ending: the stars hang there, the friends sleep, a single lamp burns in the cottage window, and only when someone opens the page does the sun come up, with everyone yawning awake.
ideas.form: the world's clock is held by the visitor's presence: time itself changes with the human

ideas.title: Echoes
ideas.idea: The cliffs on the north shore answer back: anything shouted near them comes back a second later, softer and a little wrong ('Berries!' ... 'Ferries?'), and the friends start having conversations with the echo, which slowly gets bolder.
ideas.form: a place on the island that talks back, a running joke between creatures and the land

ideas.title: Leftovers
ideas.idea: Things the friends drop stay where they fall: a half-eaten berry, a paintbrush, a lost bow, a feather from my sneeze, a starfish someone got bored of. Over days the island gathers the clutter of real lives, and now and then someone finds their own lost thing again ('My bow!').
ideas.form: a persistent trail of small objects left by everything the creatures do, found again later
